page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. The system is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. This server is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 1920 GB local NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results indicate a distinct performance profile. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, ranks in the top tier (top 10%), while multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds at 1034.93 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 69.27 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip single-threaded compression and Passmark encryption, consistently align with middle-tier performance metrics.

For specialized workloads, the server exhibits limitations in large-scale processing. While LLM inference text generation for a small 135M model achieves an average speed of 207.95 tokens/sec, prompt processing for a medium 7B model drops to the bottom 25% tier at 18.32 tokens/sec. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local NVMe storage make this instance suitable for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and moderate web serving, though it is less optimal for heavy parallel computing or large-scale AI inference.

It includes a bundled 1920 GB NVMe SSD for high-capacity local storage. Performance benchmarks place its single-core CPU capabilities in the top 10% tier, while multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations align with the middle 50% average. The server provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads and database hosting. However, it exhibits weaker performance in complex tasks like medium-model LLM prompt processing. This configuration is best suited for database management, memory-optimized applications, and general web serving.
